name: Epilator

lead: An epilator is an electric device with rotating tweezer-like discs or springs that grab and pull several hairs out at the root at once. It is used for legs, arms and sometimes other areas.
Results last about three to four weeks, longer than shaving. Users report it is painful at first, and pain tends to ease with repeated use.

paras: Mechanical tweezing pulls hair out of the follicle, so the new hair must grow from beneath the skin before it appears.

Pain, redness, ingrown hairs and folliculitis are common. Reviews find all non-permanent methods have comparable risks, and a study found no significant difference in folliculitis between manual and electric epilation. Evidence is limited, and a hair removal literature review lists epilation among temporary methods.
